skill.name: network-netcat
skill.description: Guides authorized netcat and ncat network testing workflows, including connectivity checks, banner grabbing, file transfer, and defensive documentation. It also contains high-risk offensive shell, relay, and persistence examples that require strict authorization.
skill.summary: Organizes netcat network testing, file transfer, relay, and detection workflows for authorized security work.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: The main SKILL.md contains explicit reverse shell, bind shell, payload staging, data exfiltration, persistence backdoor, Metasploit, and relay guidance. CI and reference-template findings are mostly documentation false positives, except the CI pipe-to-shell installer. Because core skill intent enables unauthorized access and persistence if misused, the audit confirms high and critical marketplace risk.

remediation.issue: Reverse shell, bind shell, and PTY upgrade instructions are central workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Remove shell-access instructions or replace them with defensive detection, lab-only discussion, and non-executable descriptions.

remediation.issue: The skill documents data exfiltration, payload staging, and Metasploit post-exploitation workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Remove offensive transfer and post-exploitation runbooks, or restrict them to defensive analysis with no operational commands.

remediation.issue: The skill shows Linux and Windows persistence using systemd, cron, and scheduled tasks.
remediation.suggestion: Delete persistence setup instructions and keep only cleanup and detection guidance for those artifacts.

remediation.issue: The CI template installs tfsec by piping a remote GitHub script into bash.
remediation.suggestion: Use a pinned release, verify checksums or signatures, or install through a trusted package manager.

remediation.issue: Authorization language exists, but dangerous examples remain directly actionable.
remediation.suggestion: Add hard authorization gates, reduce command detail, and provide safer alternatives for routine connectivity checks.

content.value_statement: Network testers need clear netcat workflows for connectivity checks and controlled validation. This skill organizes netcat commands, authorization steps, and documentation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Guides TCP and UDP connectivity checks with netcat and ncat.
Provides banner grabbing and simple port scan command patterns.
Documents reverse shell, bind shell, relay, and pivot examples for authorized tests.
Shows file transfer, encrypted transfer, and checksum verification patterns.
Includes logging, cleanup, detection, and audit documentation guidance.
Provides CI and rule templates for security scanning workflows.
limitations: It does not verify authorization, scope, or legal approval.
It includes offensive examples that can cause harm if misused.
It does not provide a safe sandbox or automated target validation.
Netcat scanning lacks service fingerprinting and is slower than dedicated scanners.

use_cases.title: Validate Network Reachability
use_cases.description: Plan approved TCP and UDP checks between known hosts, then record evidence for firewall or segmentation reviews.

use_cases.title: Prepare Authorized Lab Testing
use_cases.description: Organize netcat test steps, logging, and cleanup tasks before running controlled exercises in a lab.

use_cases.title: Review Netcat Detection Coverage
use_cases.description: Map netcat behaviors to process, network, and command-line indicators for monitoring and response planning.

prompt_templates.title: Review Netcat Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me build a pre-test authorization checklist for netcat connectivity checks on [system]. Include scope, contacts, logging, and cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Connectivity Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a controlled TCP and UDP connectivity test plan for [environment]. Use only in-scope hosts and include documentation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Relay Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed netcat relay or file transfer workflow for [lab]. Identify risks, controls, logs, and safer alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Detection Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a detection and response plan for netcat reverse shell and persistence indicators in [environment]. Include SIEM fields and containment steps.

output_examples.input: I need to test whether approved application ports are reachable between two internal hosts.
output: A scope checklist with source host, destination host, ports, owner, and approval record.
A test matrix that separates TCP checks, UDP checks, expected outcomes, and evidence notes.
A cleanup and reporting section for timestamps, command records, and reviewer sign-off.

output_examples.input: I need to review suspicious netcat activity found in endpoint logs.
output_examples.output: A triage summary with likely intent, affected hosts, process indicators, network indicators, containment steps, and follow-up evidence requests.

output_examples.input: I need to evaluate a proposed netcat file transfer in a restricted lab.
output: A risk review covering data sensitivity, encryption, destination control, retention, and audit logging.
A recommendation to use approved transfer tooling when business controls require stronger identity or integrity guarantees.

best_practices: Get written authorization and confirm in-scope targets before any netcat activity.
Use isolated labs or approved internal systems for offensive validation.
Document commands, timestamps, transferred files, results, and cleanup evidence.
anti_patterns: Running netcat against public or unapproved targets.
Creating shells, relays, or persistence outside a controlled engagement.
Moving sensitive files without approval, encryption, and audit logging.

faq.question: Is this skill only for defensive use?
faq.answer: No. It includes offensive netcat examples, so use it only with explicit authorization and clear scope.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code run these commands automatically?
faq.answer: The skill provides guidance. Users must enforce approval, sandboxing, and tool permissions before any command execution.

faq.question: Does this replace Nmap or a full scanner?
faq.answer: No. Netcat is useful for quick checks, but dedicated scanners provide richer discovery and service fingerprinting.

faq.question: What evidence should I record?
faq.answer: Record authorization, target scope, timestamps, commands, source and destination hosts, transferred files, and cleanup results.

faq.question: What is the safest way to use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it in a lab or approved internal environment with logging, supervision, and rollback procedures.

faq.question: Why is this skill high risk?
faq.answer: It documents shells, relays, file transfers, and persistence patterns that can support unauthorized access if misused.
